review_trigger: Structural capsid marker; verification of leaky-late (L1) vs true-late (L2)
measured_assay: 35S-methionine metabolic labeling, PAA arrest, 4sU-seq nascent RNA, SILAC LC-MS/MS
biological_rationale: VP5 transcription begins early (~2 hpi) and accumulates ~25% of uninhibited levels in the presence of PAA. Protein synthesis accelerates markedly following DNA replication, fulfilling the classic Honess & Roizman definition of leaky-late (gamma-1).

standard_product: Capsid maturation protease (UL26, 635 aa) / Capsid scaffold protein (UL26.5 / VP22a, 329 aa)
review_trigger: Overlapping in-frame reading frames sharing C-terminus with distinct promoters
experimental_evidence: Honess & Roizman 1974, 1975; Rutkowski 2015; Fields Virology Ch 39
biological_rationale: Both transcripts initiate from nested promoters with leaky-late (gamma-1) kinetics. UL26 encodes the full-length autoproteolytic protease that cleaves UL26.5 scaffold during DNA encapsidation. Both loci exhibit identical temporal kinetic classification.

review_trigger: Diploid terminal/internal repeat locus; complex transcriptional kinetics
experimental_evidence: Chou & Roizman 1990; Rutkowski 2015; Fields Virology Ch 39
biological_rationale: Transcribed antisense to LAT within inverted repeats. While promoter possesses late elements, expression timing varies dramatically across cell types (permissive epithelial vs post-mitotic neuronal cells). Must remain quarantined from strict single-label benchmark.

standard_product: Alpha trans-inducing factor (VP16) / Virion host shutoff protein (vhs)
review_trigger: Physical protein presence at 0 hpi via tegument delivery vs de novo synthesis timing
biological_rationale: Both proteins enter host cells packaged inside incoming virions (executing host shutoff and IE transactivation at 0 hpi). However, de novo viral transcription and new protein synthesis initiate with leaky-late (gamma-1) kinetics. Benchmark strictly annotates de novo temporal synthesis.
